title: Count Vowels
prompt: A pronunciation helper wants to know how many vowel sounds are in a word or phrase. Write a function that counts a, e, i, o, and u in the string, ignoring case.

explanation.beginner:
Example: countVowels("education") produces 5. Normalize case if required, then let each character contribute one when it is a vowel. Repeated vowels contribute repeatedly.

Compare “ignores consonants”: input ["rhythm"] produces 0. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Normalize case if required, then let each character contribute one when it is a vowel. Repeated vowels contribute repeatedly.

Tempting mistake: Counting distinct vowel types with a Set answers a different question from counting occurrences.

The reference uses includes. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost. A scan takes O(n) time with constant-sized vowel membership storage.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “ignores consonants”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
